recipes.name: Basic White Bread
recipes.description: A soft, golden sandwich loaf with a tender crumb.

less.note: Sugar is only a small supporting ingredient here: it feeds the yeast a little and helps browning, so the reduction is modest - about 25%.

steps.title: Activate the Yeast
steps.text: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and leave for 5 minutes, until foamy. If it does not foam, start again with fresh yeast.

steps.title: Make the Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the foamy yeast mixture and melted butter and stir until a shaggy dough forms.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8-10 minutes (or 5-6 minutes in a stand mixer with a dough hook) until smooth and elastic.

steps.title: First Rise
steps.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Gently press the dough into a rectangle, roll it up tightly and place it seam-side down in your greased pan ({pan}).

steps.title: Second Rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise for 30-45 minutes, until the dough crowns about 2.5 cm (1 in) above the rim of the pan.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Turn the loaf out onto a wire rack and cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

tips: Water that is too hot kills yeast - it should feel comfortably warm, not hot.
A warm, draft-free spot (such as the oven with only the light on) helps the dough rise.
Flour the surface lightly - too much extra flour makes the loaf dense.

recipes.name: Milk Bread
recipes.description: Extra soft, slightly sweet bread with a fluffy, pull-apart crumb.

less.note: Milk bread is meant to be lightly sweet and soft; a 25% reduction keeps the soft crumb while tasting less sweet.
expectedChanges: Slightly less sweet with a paler crust

profileOverrides.cook: Bake the loaf at {temp} for {time}. If the top browns quickly, tent loosely with foil after about 20 minutes.
profileOverrides.check: The loaf should be deep golden, sound hollow when you tap the bottom, and read about 93-99°C / 200-210°F in the center.
notes: The sugar and milk make the crust brown quickly - keep an eye on it.
Let the loaf cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Activate the Yeast
steps.text: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes, until foamy.

steps.title: Make the Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt. Add the foamy milk, the egg and the softened butter and stir until a shaggy dough forms.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead for about 10 minutes (or 6-8 in a stand mixer) until very smooth, stretchy and slightly tacky.

steps.title: First Rise
steps.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Gently press the dough into a rectangle, roll it up tightly and place it seam-side down in your greased pan ({pan}).

steps.title: Second Rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise for 30-45 minutes, until the dough crowns above the rim of the pan.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush the top with a little melted butter, then turn the loaf out onto a wire rack and cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

tips: The dough is soft and a little sticky - resist adding lots of extra flour.
Use whole milk for the softest crumb.
Wrapped well, the loaf stays soft for 2-3 days.

small 8×4 in / 20×10 cm loaf pan - check a few minutes early

recipes.name: Banana Bread
recipes.description: Moist, tender banana loaf with golden edges.

less.note: Ripe bananas supply lots of natural sweetness, so this loaf tolerates about 30% less sugar very well.
expectedChanges: Loaf stays moist thanks to the bananas

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, mash the bananas well, then stir in the sugar, melted butter, egg and vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the dry ingredients to the banana mixture and stir until just combined. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a wire rack. Cool before slicing.

tips: The blacker the banana skins, the sweeter and more flavorful the bread.
Mix just until the flour disappears - overmixing makes banana bread tough.
Slice a banana lengthwise and lay it on top before baking for a bakery look.

recipes.name: Cinnamon Bread
recipes.description: A tender quick loaf with a ribbon of cinnamon sugar through the middle.

less.note: Sugar appears in both the batter and the cinnamon swirl, so both are reduced by about 25%.
expectedChanges: The swirl is a little less sweet and sticky

profileOverrides.prep: Grease your pan ({pan}) and line it with parchment paper, leaving an overhang to lift the loaf out.
profileOverrides.cook: Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the top. Bake at {temp} for {time}, until golden and risen.
profileOverrides.check: A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
notes: If the top browns too fast, tent loosely with foil.
Smaller pans bake faster - start checking early.

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt and the batter sugar.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the egg, milk, melted butter and vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.

steps.title: Add the Cinnamon Swirl
steps.text: Stir the brown sugar and cinnamon together. Spread half the batter in the pan, sprinkle with half the cinnamon sugar, add the rest of the batter and top with the remaining cinnamon sugar. Swirl once or twice with a knife.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a wire rack. Cool before slicing.

tips: Do not stir the swirl too much - a couple of passes with a knife is enough.
A cinnamon-sugar sprinkle on top gives a crunchy crust.
This loaf is best the day it is made, but toasts beautifully the next day.

recipes.name: Simple Dinner Rolls

less.note: Rolls only need a little sugar; reducing it by about 25% is barely noticeable.

steps.title: Activate the Yeast
steps.text: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes, until foamy.

steps.title: Make the Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt. Add the foamy milk, egg and melted butter and stir until a shaggy dough forms.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead for 8-10 minutes (or 5-6 in a stand mixer) until smooth and elastic.

steps.title: First Rise
steps.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.

steps.title: Shape the Rolls
steps.text: Divide the dough into equal pieces (about 4 rolls for every cup of flour) and roll each into a smooth ball. Arrange them close together, just touching, in your greased pan ({pan}).

steps.title: Second Rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise for 30 minutes, until puffy.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush the warm rolls with melted butter and serve.

tips: Rolls should just touch each other so they rise upward and bake up soft.
Cover the dough with a damp towel while it rises so it does not dry out.
Make ahead: shape the rolls, refrigerate overnight, then let them come to room temperature before baking.

panOptions.text: 8 in / 20 cm round or square pan - about 6 rolls
two 9×13 in / 23×33 cm pans or two baking sheets
